f80001.claim: Canada advises to take normal security precautions in Aruba (updated 2026-10-14)

f80013.claim: Healthcare in Aruba is very good with well-equipped medical facilities

f80014.claim: Medical facilities may require immediate cash payment

f80024.claim: Aruba lies in the southern Caribbean, just outside the hurricane belt.

f80025.claim: Aruba is 19.6 miles long and six miles across.

f80028.claim: Arikok National Park, in the heart of Aruba, protects a landscape of desert sand, towering cacti and natural wonders.

f80029.claim: Aruba lies in the southern Caribbean Sea, about 15 to 18 miles north of Venezuela's Paraguaná peninsula.

f80032.claim: Aruba's currency is the Aruban florin (AWG), and US dollars are accepted in most places.

f80033.claim: Aruba's climate is tropical semi-arid, warm and sunny year-round with occasional brief rainfall.

f80035.claim: Oranjestad, Aruba's capital, has colourful colonial architecture, museums and markets.

f80037.claim: Dutch and Papiamento are Aruba's official languages, and most Arubans also speak English and Spanish.

f80048.claim: Queen Beatrix International Airport has frequent nonstop or single-connection flights from most major US cities and daily flights from major hubs around the world.

f80049.claim: American, Canadian, Caribbean, European and most South American citizens do not need visas to enter Aruba.

f80050.claim: A valid passport is required to enter Aruba, and anyone using false documents faces legal action.

f80051.claim: Visitors to Aruba are asked to fill out the Embarkation-Disembarkation Card online.

f80052.claim: Aruba has more than 20 public beaches and coves.

f80054.claim: In Aruba, visitors can take a taxi, use public transportation or arrange a shuttle to and from hotels, resorts and attractions.

f80055.claim: The bus is an informal and inexpensive way to see Aruba.

f80057.claim: Visitors can rent a car, motorcycle or scooter at Aruba's airport.

f80063.claim: A rechargeable card pays for parking in and around Oranjestad.

f80066.claim: Aruba's tourism authority asks travellers to check its traveller requirements page before they travel, as it keeps updating details of the sustainability fee.

f80067.claim: Visitors are asked to leave shells, coral and other natural materials on Aruba.

f80069.claim: Aruba's hotels and resorts are concentrated along the island's northwestern coast.

f80070.claim: Aruba has high-rise hotels in Palm Beach and low-rise resorts near the quieter Eagle Beach.

f80082.claim: Visitors are asked to respect Aruba's Fofoti trees, coral reefs, donkeys and sea turtles.

f80084.claim: Visitors to Aruba are asked to pack mineral-based sunscreen, which may be labelled reef safe.

f80085.claim: The active ingredient of a suitable sunscreen for Aruba should be titanium dioxide or zinc oxide.

f80086.claim: Aruba's tourism authority invites visitors to drink the island's water straight from the tap.

f80087.claim: Driving on the beach is forbidden in Aruba because the beach is a fragile ecosystem.

f80088.claim: Off-roaders in Aruba are asked to drive carefully to avoid damaging the landscape or harming protected species.

f80089.claim: Aruba has banned plastic bags, plastic utensils and confetti, among other items.

f80090.claim: The Port of Aruba is steps from the shops, restaurants and pastel architecture of Oranjestad.

f80102.claim: The caves and ancient boulders of Arikok National Park can be toured on foot, on horseback or by vehicle.

f80113.claim: Every stretch of sand in Aruba is public.

f80114.claim: Aruba's west and south coasts are calm and protected, which suits swimming and snorkelling.

f80115.claim: Aruba's east and north coasts face the open sea and have stronger winds, crashing waves and scenic viewpoints.

f80117.claim: All of Aruba's beaches are open to everyone, and many can be reached by car or public bus.

f80118.claim: Eagle Beach is a long stretch of soft white sand with the famous fofoti trees.

f80119.claim: Boca Catalina is a small bay with gentle waves and colourful reef fish just offshore.

f80121.claim: Boca Grandi, on Aruba's east side, suits windsurfing and kitesurfing, but its strong current makes it a poor place to swim.

f80123.claim: Baby Beach is the most child-friendly beach in Aruba, thanks to its shallow, calm water.

f80125.claim: Public transport reaches Aruba's major beaches, while a car makes it easier to reach smaller coves.

f80126.claim: Aruba's east coast has stronger waves, rugged terrain and fewer crowds, and is better for photos and exploring than for swimming.

f80127.claim: Beachgoers who want free shade under public palapas should arrive early.

f80128.claim: Visitors to Aruba's beaches are asked not to feed wildlife and never to stand on reefs.

f80163.claim: Nearly 20 per cent of Aruba is designated National Park.

f80165.claim: Arikok National Park's attractions include caves, original Indian rock drawings and land formations made from lava, quartz diorite and limestone.

f80166.claim: Most tours of Arikok National Park are guided by park rangers.

f80167.claim: Visitors need to buy a ticket to enter Arikok National Park.

f80168.claim: Hooiberg is the Dutch word for haystack.

f80169.claim: Hooiberg is cone-shaped and rises 540 feet from the centre of Aruba.

f80170.claim: About 600 steps lead to the top of Hooiberg.

f80171.claim: The Ayo and Casibari Rock Formations are open to climb and explore.

f80172.claim: The area of the Ayo Rock Formations was once considered a sacred site by Aruba's original inhabitants.

f80173.claim: Original rock drawings dating back thousands of years can be found at the Ayo Rock Formations.

f80174.claim: Baby Beach is in the south of Aruba, close to San Nicolas.

f80175.claim: Baby Beach is a half-moon of sand on a calm lagoon, suited to families with small children.

f80176.claim: Where the bay at Baby Beach opens to the ocean, snorkellers are asked to stay within the marked snorkel area.

f80178.claim: Baby Beach is about a 45-minute drive from the Palm Beach hotels.

f80179.claim: Arashi Beach is on the northern tip of Aruba, just beyond Malmok on the road to the California Lighthouse.

f80180.claim: Arashi Beach has car parking, public transport, a beach bar, shaded huts and chair rentals.

f80181.claim: The best snorkelling at Arashi Beach is on the left side when facing the sea.

f80182.claim: Mangel Halto is a secluded beach with calm, shallow water rich in sea life and a network of mangroves.

f80189.claim: Fort Zoutman is the oldest remaining building in Oranjestad.

f80190.claim: Fort Zoutman, named after Dutch Rear Admiral Johan Arnold Zoutman, was completed in 1798 after two years of construction.

f80191.claim: The Willem III Tower beside Fort Zoutman was built in 1868 and served as both a lighthouse and a public clock tower.

f80193.claim: Zeerover is a local fishermen's wharf in Savaneta serving fresh seafood cleaned and cooked in front of customers.

f80197.claim: The transformation of San Nicolas into Aruba's Art District began in 2016.

f80198.claim: San Nicolas has murals by local and international artists.

f80199.claim: Aruba Mural Tours start at the ArtisA, or Art is Aruba, gallery.

f80200.claim: Temperatures in Aruba average between 80°F and 90°F, or 27°C to 32°C, through the year, and rain is rare.

f80202.claim: Even in Aruba's rainy season, a whole day of rain is rare.

f80203.claim: Aruba has three main weather seasons: the rainy season from October to December, the dry season from January to April and the windy season from May to October.

f80204.claim: Hi-Winds Aruba, the annual kiteboarding and windsurfing competition, takes place in May.

f80205.claim: Aruba lies well south of the main Atlantic hurricane belt, and hurricanes there are extremely rare.

f80206.claim: During the Caribbean hurricane season from June to November, Aruba can feel side effects from hurricanes passing through the region.

f80207.claim: Aruba's off-season runs from September to November.

f80208.claim: Aruba's peak season runs from December to April.

f80209.claim: Aruba's hurricane season runs from 1 June to 30 November.

f80210.claim: Carnival season in January and February is a popular time to visit Aruba.

f80212.claim: Aruba's off-season months bring a higher chance of sporadic rain and a higher heat index.

f80213.claim: Aruba's off-season brings substantial savings on accommodation, flights, rental cars and activities, along with smaller crowds.

f80214.claim: Some businesses and restaurants in Aruba may close for renovations or holidays in the off-season.

f80216.claim: In peak season Aruba gets busy, and prices for accommodation and activities tend to be higher.

f80224.claim: In Papiamento, bon dia, bon tardi and bon nochi mean good morning, good afternoon and good evening.

f80225.claim: Aruba runs on Atlantic Standard Time.

f80226.claim: Aruba has no daylight saving time.

f80228.claim: Buses run every 15 minutes from 5.45 a.m. until 6 p.m., then every 40 minutes until 11.30 p.m.

f80229.claim: The central bus station in downtown Oranjestad is next to the cruise terminal and Royal Plaza.

f80231.claim: Aruba's public buses do not run 24 hours a day.

f80235.claim: Arubus buses do not take luggage, only carry-on items.

f80236.claim: Arubus routes L10A, L10B and L10C run along the hotel strip, stopping at beaches including Eagle Beach, Palm Beach and Arashi Beach.

f80242.claim: British citizens can visit Aruba for up to 3 months without a visa.

f80244.claim: Travellers must show the airline proof of approval to travel before flying to Aruba.

f80245.claim: Anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty must be declared on entering or leaving Aruba.

f80246.claim: Travellers passing through Aruba in transit also need to fill in the embarkation/disembarkation card.

f80247.claim: Aruba has a risk of petty theft and occasional incidents of street crime.

f80248.claim: The UK government advises not taking valuables or cash to the beach in Aruba.

f80249.claim: Carrying ID is a legal requirement in Aruba.

f80252.claim: Hire car companies in Aruba often have stricter requirements, such as 2 years of driving experience, a higher minimum age and an international driving permit.

f80253.claim: Drink-driving is a serious offence in Aruba.

f80254.claim: To avoid being overcharged by a taxi, agree the fare in local currency with the driver before setting off.

f80257.claim: The European Health Insurance Card and the Global Health Insurance Card are not valid in Aruba.

f80258.claim: The UK government advises adequate travel health insurance and accessible funds to cover medical treatment and repatriation.

f80259.claim: Aruba's emergency numbers are 911 for ambulance and fire, 100 for police and 913 for the coastguard.

f80260.claim: All arriving passengers must clear immigration before entering Aruba.

f80262.claim: Eligible travellers can use e-gates for faster immigration processing at Aruba's airport.

f80267.claim: Every traveller to Aruba, including infants and children, must complete and get approval for the ED-Card.

f80268.claim: The ED-Card can be filled out within seven days before the trip.

f80269.claim: From 1 July 2024, Aruba applies a $20 Sustainability Fee to visitors arriving by air.

f80281.claim: Aruba's Carnival is a months-long celebration and the island's biggest party of the year.
